title: Design governance
learningObjective: Recommend a structure of management groups, subscriptions and resource groups with a tagging strategy, a compliance solution, and an identity governance solution.
foundation: Governance keeps a growing Azure estate organised, compliant and affordable.
Think of four levels: management groups (rules for many subscriptions), subscriptions (billing and limits), resource groups (things that live and die together) and tags (labels for reporting).
Then decide how to enforce rules (Azure Policy), prove compliance, and keep people's access right over time.
engineer: Hierarchy: keep management groups shallow (up to six levels below the tenant root) and organised by policy needs, not the org chart. The Azure landing zone reference uses Platform (Identity, Management, Connectivity), Landing zones (Corp, Online), Sandbox and Decommissioned. Subscriptions are units of scale, billing and isolation (quotas, limits, RBAC boundary); separate production from non-production. Resource groups hold resources with the same lifecycle; a resource belongs to one group.

Tagging: define a small mandatory set (for example CostCenter, Environment, Owner, Application) and enforce it with Azure Policy (Require a tag, Inherit a tag from the resource group or subscription with Modify). Tags are not inherited by default. Cost Management can group and allocate costs by tag.

Compliance: Azure Policy initiatives (built-in regulatory initiatives such as ISO 27001, NIST, PCI DSS) assigned at management groups with Deny, Audit, Modify and DeployIfNotExists; exemptions for justified exceptions; Defender for Cloud's regulatory compliance dashboard to report; resource locks for critical resources; Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager for Microsoft 365 and data compliance. Azure Blueprints is deprecated: use template specs, deployment stacks and policy instead.

Identity governance (Microsoft Entra ID Governance / P2): access reviews (recurring certification of group, app and role access, including guests), entitlement management (access packages with approval, expiry and connected organisations), Privileged Identity Management, lifecycle workflows (joiner-mover-leaver automation) and terms of use.

animation.caption: Decide where each governance control belongs and which tool proves compliance.

example.title: A landing-zone hierarchy for a holding company
body: Under the tenant root: Platform (identity, management, connectivity subscriptions), Landing zones with Corp and Online, Sandbox and Decommissioned. 'Allowed locations' and 'Require tag CostCenter' are assigned at the top management group; Corp denies public IPs.
Quarterly access reviews remove guests who no longer need access, contractors get time-limited access packages, and lifecycle workflows disable leavers on their last day.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: Management groups: create the hierarchy and move subscriptions.
Policy > Assignments: assign initiatives at management groups; Exemptions.
Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity governance: access reviews, entitlement management, lifecycle workflows.
configuration.cli:
az account management-group create --name mg-landingzones --parent mg-contoso
az policy assignment create --name require-costcenter --scope /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/mg-contoso \
  --policy "Require a tag on resources" --params '{"tagName":{"value":"CostCenter"}}'

troubleshooting.symptom: Cost reports show many resources with no CostCenter.
troubleshooting.cause: Tags not enforced, and not inherited.
troubleshooting.fix: Assign 'Require a tag' (Deny) for new resources and 'Inherit a tag from the resource group' (Modify) with remediation.

troubleshooting.symptom: A policy blocks a justified exception for one sandbox.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a policy exemption (Waiver) with an expiry date.

comparisons.difference: Management groups organise and apply policy/RBAC; subscriptions are the billing, quota and isolation boundary.
Access reviews certify existing access periodically; PIM makes privileged access just-in-time.

misconceptions.myth: Tags flow down from resource groups automatically.

misconceptions.reality: Design them around policy and access needs.

walkthrough.subtitle: Organise subscriptions so rules, costs and access stay under control as you grow.

A tagging strategy enforced by policy

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: Forty subscriptions and no rules
body: Resources appear in any region, nobody knows who pays, and old access never goes away.

steps.label: Hierarchy
steps.title: Four levels, four jobs
body: Management groups: apply policy and access to many subscriptions. Subscriptions: billing and limits. Resource groups: things deployed and deleted together. Tags: labels for reports.

callout.text: Organise management groups by the rules they need, not by the org chart.

steps.label: Tags
steps.title: A small, enforced set of tags
body: Choose a few mandatory tags (CostCenter, Environment, Owner). Azure Policy requires them on new resources and can copy them from the resource group, because tags are not inherited by themselves.

steps.label: Compliance
steps.title: Enforce with policy, report with Defender
body: Assign built-in regulatory initiatives at management groups. Defender for Cloud shows how you score against standards like ISO 27001 or PCI DSS.

steps.label: People
steps.title: Identity governance
body: Access reviews ask owners every quarter whether access is still needed. Access packages give time-limited bundles of access. PIM keeps admin rights just-in-time. Lifecycle workflows handle joiners and leavers.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Governance design
recap: MG = policy/RBAC; subscription = billing; RG = lifecycle; tags = reporting
Access reviews, access packages, PIM, lifecycle workflows

handsOn.title: Enforce a rule with Azure Policy and watch it block a deployment
handsOn.cost: Free. Policy assignments and compliance scans cost nothing.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription. Work in a resource group called rg-az305-lab.
If rg-az305-lab does not exist yet: Resource groups > Create > name rg-az305-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Search 'Policy' > Assignments > Assign policy. Scope: your subscription, resource group rg-az305-lab. Policy definition: search 'Allowed locations'.
steps.tip: Assigning at a resource group keeps the lab from affecting anything else. In a real design you'd assign at a management group.

steps.do: Parameters: Allowed locations = only your lab region. Review + create > Create.
steps.see: The assignment appears; it can take up to 30 minutes to take effect, usually less.

steps.do: Try to create a storage account in rg-az305-lab in a DIFFERENT region (for example West US).
steps.tip: This is a Deny effect: the request is stopped before anything is created.

steps.do: Create the storage account again in your lab region (any unique name, Standard LRS).

steps.see: Resources listed as compliant; a scan may take a while to appear.

steps.do: Policy > Assignments > select it > Create exemption (look but don't save).
steps.see: Exemption options: Waiver or Mitigated, with an expiry date.

check: The out-of-region deployment was blocked; the in-region one worked.
cleanup: Policy > Assignments: delete the Allowed locations assignment.
Resource groups > rg-az305-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete.
